questions.explanation: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor at the end of the aerobic electron transport chain. It accepts electrons and protons to form water, and this final acceptance permits electron flow through the chain to continue normally.

options.text: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it accepts electrons and protons to form water, allowing electron flow through the aerobic chain to continue.
Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it donates electrons and protons to form water, allowing electron flow through the aerobic chain to continue.
Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it accepts electrons and protons to form carbon dioxide, allowing electron flow through the aerobic chain to continue.
Oxygen is the first electron acceptor; it accepts electrons and protons to form water, allowing electron flow through the aerobic chain to continue.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains oxygen’s role in the aerobic electron transport chain?
